output.logline: Across five documentary-style chapters, a lone field archivist and a radio operator traverse a continent of immaculate, abandoned metropolises where every clock stopped before dawn and no citizen ever woke, assembling visual evidence of a civilization suspended in perfect stillness.

characters.name: Mara Voss
characters.visual_description: Woman in her late 30s, tall and lean with weathered pale skin, narrow grey eyes, a straight nose, and dark ash-brown hair cut to jaw length and tucked behind both ears. She wears a charcoal waxed-cotton field jacket with a stand collar turned down, front brass zipper fully closed under a snapped storm placket, two bellows chest pockets and two hip pockets; a faded black crew-neck merino sweater under the jacket; dark olive straight-leg cargo trousers with stitched knee panels; a matte black web belt with a rectangular steel buckle; brown full-grain leather lace-up combat boots with scuffed toes; thin black leather gloves; and a compact 16 mm still camera hanging from a black canvas neck strap at mid sternum.

characters.name: Elias Reed
characters.visual_description: Man in his early 40s, broad-shouldered and medium height with deep brown skin, a shaved head, heavy brows, a square jaw, and a short salt-and-pepper beard trimmed close to the face. He wears a sand-colored canvas expedition parka with hood folded flat, front zipper fully closed to the throat, snapped cuff tabs, and large lower patch pockets; a slate blue henley shirt under the parka with three dark buttons fastened; dark brown utility trousers with plain straight legs; a thick tan leather shoulder holster carrying a handheld radio at the left rib; black rubberized field watch on the left wrist; and dark umber lug-sole lace-up work boots dusted with pale grit.

objects.name: Survey wagon
objects.visual_description: Boxy long-wheelbase expedition station wagon, matte faded olive paint over steel body panels, black tubular roof rack, reinforced front bumper with a central winch, round headlamps protected by wire guards, a vertical whip antenna fixed to the right rear corner, rear side windows covered from inside by wire mesh, and both front doors marked with a small off-white stencil reading ARCHIVE SURVEY UNIT 3. The left rear quarter panel carries a scrape of exposed metal and the rear hatch has a dent above the handle.

objects.name: Shortwave field radio
objects.visual_description: Rectangular handheld shortwave transceiver in dark olive ribbed casing, black rubber antenna nearly forearm length, silver frequency dial window, two knurled black knobs on the top edge, a coiled cord leading to a square speaker microphone clipped to the chest, and a strip of cracked white tape on the back handwritten with the letters ER-2 in black ink.

objects.name: Stopped station clock
objects.visual_description: Large circular public clock with a brushed aluminum bezel, yellowed cream face, thick black minute marks, blunt black hour and minute hands fixed at 4:17, thin red second hand bent slightly near the tip, and hairline cracks spreading from the center arbor under dusty glass.

locations.name: Terminal City Central Station — dawn stillness
locations.visual_description: Vast Beaux-Arts rail terminal interior with a barrel-vaulted ceiling and a central concourse the size of a cathedral nave. At the center stands an information kiosk of dark green painted iron under the stopped station clock fixed high above it. On the left, six silent ticket windows sit beneath brass destination boards; on the right, a row of wooden benches faces a tiled wall with enamel route maps. In the background, three arched track portals open into blue dawn haze and motionless trains. The floor is pale stone in a black geometric pattern, scattered with abandoned newspapers and a single toppled suitcase, and every lamp globe remains lit with weak amber current.

locations.name: Terminal City Financial District — noon dust
locations.visual_description: Broad six-lane avenue running straight toward a canyon of Art Deco and glass office towers, the street empty except for stalled cars angled at traffic lights. At the center rises a black granite bank tower with a stepped crown and rows of dark windows; on the left stands a bronze statue plaza ringed by dead fountains and low hedge planters; on the right a department store with striped awnings and shattered revolving doors spills mannequins into display windows. In the background, elevated tram cables cross between towers and disappear into white noon dust. The asphalt is filmed with windblown paper, sand, and dry leaves, and every pedestrian signal still shows red.

locations.name: Harbor Megacity Seawall — storm front
locations.visual_description: Long concrete seawall curving around a drowned commercial harbor under an immense industrial skyline. At the center, a rust-streaked ferry terminal canopy projects over a deserted embarkation platform; on the left, stacked cargo cranes stand skeletal over silent container yards; on the right, apartment slabs and hotel towers rise in dense layers behind a flooded boulevard lined with bent palms. In the background, a suspension bridge fades into rain bands over dark water. The seawall surface is slick with standing water, torn warning flags, and blown kelp, while waves strike the barrier in white bursts beneath a green-black storm sky.

locations.name: Capitol Ring Road — night under emergency light
locations.visual_description: Multi-level circular motorway interchange surrounding a monumental government district, seen from an elevated overpass. At the center, a broad ceremonial boulevard leads to a domed parliament building faced in pale stone and fronted by rows of unlit flagpoles. On the left, stacked flyover ramps curl over immobilized buses and sedans; on the right, a line of ministry blocks with repetitive colonnades and dark window grids stretches toward a radio mast blinking red. In the background, the skyline recedes into blackout except for sporadic emergency beacons. The road surface shines with recent rain, lane markings reflect harsh sodium-orange spill, and abandoned vehicles sit exactly in their lanes with doors closed.

locations.name: Sunken Residential Quarter — final blue dawn
locations.visual_description: Flooded residential district of mid-rise apartment blocks and narrow cross streets viewed from a rooftop edge. At the center, a straight canal-like street has replaced the avenue below, with half-submerged cars and floating furniture aligned between building facades. On the left, a brick schoolhouse with a clock turret rises above the waterline and its playground fence disappears into the flood; on the right, laundry balconies and external fire stairs cling to stained concrete apartment buildings with windows standing open and curtains hanging still. In the background, a distant skyline of towers emerges from ground fog as first light turns the horizon steel blue. Rooftop gravel, vent pipes, and a toppled satellite dish frame the foreground, and the water below lies unnaturally glassy without ripples or birds.

continuity_rules: Keep Mara Voss and Elias Reed in the exact same outfits in every scene.
The stopped station clock always reads 4:17 whenever any clock face is visible.
The survey wagon always appears with matte faded olive paint, wire-guard headlamps, roof rack, and left rear scrape.
Frame people as small figures against oversized civic or industrial geometry.
No crowds, bodies, or active civilians ever appear; the cities are completely unawakened.
Weather must progress by chapter: dawn haze, noon dust, storm, wet night, final blue dawn.
Use only the five listed locations in chronological chapter order from Central Station to Sunken Residential Quarter.
Maintain documentary realism in architecture and props even while the cessation event remains unexplained.

generations.text:
[CHAPTER 1: The Count Before Silence]
At the drowned quarter, Mara stops the wagon and gives Elias twelve battery minutes. He rigs the shortwave at the curb while she wades three buildings, loses one reel case, and keeps the count. On the third landing, a battery clock holds the same pre-dawn minute as the station, towers, seawall, and ring road. She calls Elias to witness, log, and transmit before the district current fails. Another grid section dies as she seals the archive.

By the next blue dawn, Elias sends one burst: five cities checked, one minute repeated, one archive secured. Mara and Elias leave with proof the stoppage reached the continent, and the count survives.
